clue.text: Allegorist's work written after deep reflection

indicators.note: the piece for work is placed after the reflected piece
a reflection shows a thing mirrored, so the word for deep is read backwards

parts.note: the deep is a poetic name for the sea
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: An allegorical writer's book, composed after long and serious thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflection' turns SEA into AES; the 's of 'Allegorist's' is just 'is' linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek fabulist told moral tales with animal characters, which are allegories.

clue.text: Great enjoyment from a superior type of dancing

parts.note: high means superior or elevated
old-time dancing is a traditional ballroom style

explanation.surface: Someone gets great pleasure from a classy style of dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a thoroughly enjoyable occasion, a really good spree.

clue.text: Youngster departs leaving trunk beside train

parts.note: to school someone is to train them

indicators.note: the departs abbreviation goes out of the word for trunk

parts.note: the trunk is the torso, the body
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A young person leaves, abandoning a suitcase next to a railway train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' and 'train' look like luggage and railway; they are BODY and SCHOOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil at school is by definition a young person.

clue.text: Remove press, under pressure

indicators.note: in a down answer the press piece sits beneath the pressure piece

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
to press someone is to urge them

explanation.surface: An instruction to get rid of the newspapers while under strain.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear out unwanted elements or people is to get rid of them, a synonym of remove.

clue.text: Most resentful, driven to extremes by Anglican priest

indicators.note: only the far ends of the phrase Anglican priest are kept, its middle pushed out

explanation.surface: A churchman pushed to the limit becomes the most bitter of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driven to extremes' keeps ANG and RIEST, dropping LICANP from the middle of 'Anglican priest'.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of cross or furious, matching the superlative 'most resentful'.

clue.text: Genuine article received by BBC missing last chapter

indicators.note: the article goes inside the trimmed nickname for the BBC
the final letter of the nickname is dropped

parts.note: Auntie (or Auntie Beeb) is a British nickname for the BBC
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A real feature accepted by the BBC, though lacking its final chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: Auntie is a long-standing affectionate British nickname for the BBC; 'missing last' drops its E before the article goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something authentic is real and not fake, so genuine is a direct synonym.

clue.text: On the way, I abandoned honour

indicators.note: the letter for I is given up from the word for on the way

parts.note: going means on the way, travelling

explanation.surface: Someone who gave up an award while travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: A gong is British slang for a medal or decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a medal or official award such as a knighthood.

clue.text: Awkward adjustment to get in lane

indicators.note: an adjustment rearranges the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A clumsy driving manoeuvre to move into the right lane.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking grace or polish, clumsy in manner, which is what awkward means.

clue.text: Fish glide on the surface

definitions.meaning: to move smoothly over ice on blades

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a flat ray found in the sea and the act of sliding over ice.

clue.text: Late cut imposed by government

parts.note: the late are the dead; the state takes a cut of what a dead person leaves, not a cricket stroke

explanation.surface: A cricket shot, the late cut, ordered by the government.
explanation.walkthrough: A late cut is a cricket stroke played very late; here 'late' means deceased.
explanation.definitionFit: The duty levied on an estate passing on death is the state's share of what the deceased leaves.

clue.text: Minding your own business?

parts.note: read not as keeping out of affairs but as running a firm of your own

explanation.surface: A gentle reproach to stay out of other people's affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone working for themselves rather than an employer literally runs their own business.

clue.text: Cleaned up last of goo that's hung around

indicators.note: the hung word goes round the last letter of goo

parts.note: hovered means hung in the air

indicators.note: only the final letter of goo is taken

explanation.surface: Someone cleared up the remaining sticky mess that had been lingering.
explanation.definitionFit: To vacuum, using the brand name of a well-known vacuum cleaner as a verb.

clue.text: Church of England deacon's first in diocese to pull out

indicators.note: the church letters and the deacon's initial go inside the word for diocese

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese

indicators.note: only the opening letter of deacon is taken

explanation.surface: An Anglican deacon is the first in the diocese to break away.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw formally from a union or federation, as states may do.

clue.text: Delivers lectures after colleague's third one

indicators.note: the lecturing word comes after the other two pieces
the third letter of colleague is taken

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to berate is to scold or lecture

explanation.surface: Someone gives talks following a co-worker's third talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivers' and 'lectures' both suggest giving talks; 'delivers' means sets free.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver someone from captivity is to set them free.

clue.text: Deteriorate, as hungry hens might?

definitions.meaning: to go to seed, decline through neglect
famished poultry would dash towards grain scattered for them

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for going to pot, read literally, describes hens hurrying to their grain.

clue.text: Vessels crack up below neck

indicators.note: in a down answer the crack piece sits under the neck piece

parts.note: neck, like sauce, means cheek or impudence

indicators.note: in a down answer up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: to crack is to snap

explanation.surface: Pots breaking just beneath their necks.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooking pots are vessels, containers for holding liquid or food.

clue.text: Needing a place to go, fellow's withdrawn

parts.note: a loo is a toilet, a place to go

explanation.surface: A man who badly needs a toilet has gone quiet and retreated.
explanation.definitionFit: Distant and reserved in manner, keeping apart from others.

clue.text: With nobody coming in, Cook stood alone

indicators.note: the nobody word enters the rearranged letters
to cook something is to tamper with it, so the letters of stood are rearranged

parts.note: none means nobody

explanation.surface: No one else turns up, so a chef waits by themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is British rhyming slang: Tod Sloan, a jockey, rhymes with 'own'. 'coming in' puts the nobody word after the first letter of the rearrangement, OSTOD.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for by oneself, without company.

clue.text: Don to test lines in fashion

indicators.note: the lines abbreviation goes inside the fashion word

parts.note: ton is an old word for high fashion
RY is short for railway, lines of track

explanation.surface: A university teacher being examined on some lines of verse, in style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a university teacher; it is the verb to put on clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on a garment to see whether it fits is to don it as a test.

clue.text: Sue fell over bench here

parts.note: to court someone is to woo or sue for their hand

indicators.note: over signals the fell word turned back to front

parts.note: a fell is a moor or upland hill

explanation.surface: A woman named Sue tripped over a seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sue' looks like a name and 'fell' like tripping; they are COURT and MOOR, with 'over' reversing MOOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The bench, meaning the judges or magistrates, sits in the room where trials are heard.

clue.text: Source of milk for army medic in capital?

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, so something for him is the MO's
a cow is the usual source of milk

explanation.surface: Where to get milk for a military doctor stationed in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as the MO's cow, the army doctor's own milk supply.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian city is the nation's seat of government; the question mark flags the playful wordplay.

clue.text: Language most extreme characters used in Westminster?

indicators.note: the extreme letters are placed inside the Westminster postcode

parts.note: SW1 is the London postcode for Westminster, written with I for 1
A and Z are the first and last letters of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Some coarse language used by politicians at Westminster.
explanation.walkthrough: Westminster is the seat of the UK Parliament; its postcode is SW1.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bantu tongue of southern Africa, also called siSwati, is a language.

clue.text: Hard evidence of life in realms of Neptune and Pluto

parts.note: Neptune is the Roman god of the seas
Pluto is the Roman god of the underworld, hell

explanation.surface: Signs of life in the remote planets Neptune and Pluto.
explanation.walkthrough: Neptune and Pluto look like planets; they are the Roman gods of the sea and the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard casing left by a mollusc is a solid trace that a creature once lived there.

clue.text: Individual without husband on this?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the individual word surrounds the husband letter

parts.note: self means one's individual person

explanation.surface: Where a single person without a husband is said to be left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means 'outside'. To be 'on the shelf' is an old idiom for being unmarried.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone left unmarried was said to be on it, like goods nobody bought.

clue.text: Shaft cut, keeping close to well

indicators.note: the cut word holds the final letter of well inside it

parts.note: to axe is to cut

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A well shaft is being trimmed nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: The rod on which a wheel turns is a kind of shaft.

clue.text: Sex party: beauty shot making historic record

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Photographing a beauty at an orgy produces a memorable record.
explanation.definitionFit: The embroidered cloth chronicling the Norman conquest of England in 1066 is a famous historical record.

clue.text: Transport back in family's favour

indicators.note: the reversed transport word goes inside the family word

parts.note: kin is family, with the s kept

indicators.note: back means the transport word is read in reverse

parts.note: to send is to transport

explanation.surface: Giving relatives a lift home as a good turn to the family.
explanation.definitionFit: A favour is a kind act, a good turn shown to someone.

clue.text: Vogue journalist didn't last

parts.note: a vogue or passing craze is a fad
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A fashion magazine writer had a short career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vogue' looks like the magazine; it means a passing fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that faded lost strength and vanished, so it did not endure.
